name: Rain Yang
life: “I still remember a client thanking me in the language I hadn't put on my form.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Rain by a small Saturday habit. Rain takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I speak his language but the agency only knows I clean offices. I want to train without losing my rent money.
appearance: Rain is easy to recognize by short black hair swept back and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a brown corduroy jacket with a pen clipped inside the neckline, Rain presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Rain has a long memory for unfair prices and a short one for small insults. Rain can get along perfectly well with an enemy provided the account between them is clear.
agenda: To qualify for care work without losing rent income.
family: Edgar Joseph is Rain’s cousin raised in the same household. Rain calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Edgar leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *A ship without postcards*, Edgar says, “I draw the alley bins because my mother knows cities by their cats.”
connections: Lina Barrett. Training applications and job letters reveal two workers' long-hidden language skills.
